does.label: The four tones
does.note: mā má mǎ mà — one syllable, four words.

does.label: Initials
does.note: The consonants, including the six that English has no equivalent for.

does.label: Tone drill
does.note: Minimal pairs. Do this until you can pick the tone without thinking.

stages.goal: Hear the four tones apart and read pinyin out loud. No characters yet.
stages.title: The sounds
stages.why: Mandarin is not hard to pronounce; it is hard to hear. A learner who starts on characters before the tones spends a year storing words in a shape their ear cannot retrieve. Two or three days here saves months of that.

stages.goal: Greet someone, give your name, ask theirs, say yes, no, thank you and sorry.
stages.sentence: 你好！我叫…，你叫什么名字？
stages.title: First contact
stages.why: Thirty items, and every one of them is used in the first minute of a conversation. The old order reached 谢谢 at item 146.

stages.goal: Say where you are, where you are going, what you like, and what you can do.
stages.sentence: 我在中国学习，我很喜欢喝茶。
stages.title: People and doing things
stages.why: The verbs come next because a pronoun with no verb says nothing. After this stretch you can build a sentence rather than name a thing.

stages.goal: Count, ask a price, give your age, say the date and the time.
stages.sentence: 这个多少钱？——三十五块。
stages.title: Numbers and time
stages.why: Numbers arrive here rather than on day one. Ten digits learned before you can count anything are ten shapes with no hook; learned beside 岁, 钱 and 点 they stick on the first pass.

stages.goal: Finish HSK 1: family, food, places, weather, and the rest of the first list.
stages.sentence: 明天天气很好，我们和朋友去饭店吃饭。
stages.title: Everyday life
stages.why: The remainder of HSK 1, now ordered so that each word leans on characters you already hold. Production cards open here — writing a word from its meaning is worth the reps only once you can read it.

stages.goal: Say what you did, what you are in the middle of, and what is about to happen.
stages.sentence: 我在中国住过两年，现在正在学汉语。
stages.title: Done, doing, about to
stages.why: HSK 2 opens on aspect, because a language that can only say 我吃饭 cannot hold a conversation. 了 finishes an action, 过 records that you have ever done it, 正在 puts you inside one and 要…了 says it is coming. Four markers, one verb, four different times — and none of them is a tense.

stages.goal: Give a reason, describe how something turned out, and say where things are in relation to each other.
stages.sentence: 因为下雨，所以我没看见他。
stages.title: Reasons and results
stages.why: 因为…所以 is the first sentence with two halves, and 结果补语 is the first verb that carries its own outcome — 看见 rather than 看, 做完 rather than 做. Both are places where English gets by with one word and Chinese does not.

stages.goal: Finish HSK 2: contradict yourself politely, and say how much.
stages.sentence: 虽然有点儿贵，但是很好吃。
stages.title: Concession and degree
stages.why: 虽然…但是 keeps both halves where English drops one, and 有点儿 and 一点儿 are the pair that decides whether you are complaining or asking. 有点儿贵 is a remark about the price; 便宜一点儿 is a request.

stages.goal: Place an event in time, and describe a state that is simply holding.
stages.sentence: 我来的时候，门开着，他一直在等我。
stages.title: When, and what state it is in
stages.why: Handwriting opens here, because by now enough components are in place that a stroke order is a pattern rather than a shape to copy. So does 着 — the difference between 他在开门 and 门开着 is the difference between an action and what it left behind, and no European language marks it.

stages.goal: Set a condition, and take something out of a group.
stages.sentence: 如果明天不下雨，除了他以外我们都去。
stages.title: If, and except
stages.why: 如果…就 is the first thing that lets you talk about what has not happened, which is most of what anybody talks about. 除了…以外 is the trap: with 都 it excludes, with 还 it includes, and only the second half tells you which.

stages.goal: Say what you did to a thing, and what was done to it.
stages.sentence: 请把窗户关上，书被他拿走了。
stages.title: 把 and 被
stages.why: The two hardest patterns in HSK 3 and the reason it is the level where learners stall. 把 moves the object in front of the verb because the sentence is about what happened to it, and the verb can never then stand bare. 被 turns the sentence round. They are placed together, after the result complements they both need.

stages.goal: Finish HSK 3: chain two things together, in sequence and in addition.
stages.sentence: 他一到家就做饭，又快又好吃。
stages.title: Joining clauses
stages.why: 一…就, 先…然后, 又…又, 不但…而且. Until now a sentence has been one clause; from here it is two, and which connector you reach for is most of what makes writing sound Chinese rather than translated.

stages.goal: Correct someone, offer an alternative, and say whose view you are giving.
stages.sentence: 这不是钱的问题，而是时间的问题。
stages.title: Framing a statement
stages.why: HSK 4 is where the language stops describing and starts arguing. 不是…而是 corrects, 不是…就是 offers, 对…来说 says whose judgement it is. The distinction between 而是 and 就是 is one character and the opposite meaning.

stages.goal: Say what something depends on, how it was done, and what follows from what both people already know.
stages.sentence: 既然来不及了，就按照原来的计划做吧。
stages.title: Conditions and means
stages.why: 既然 and 因为 both give a reason, and only one of them assumes the listener already has it. 通过 and 按照 both introduce a method, and only one of them is a rule you are following. This is the level at which near-synonyms start to matter more than new words.

stages.goal: Track one thing changing with another, and narrow a claim to a part of it.
stages.sentence: 随着时间过去，光靠努力已经不够了。
stages.title: Change and scope
stages.why: 随着 ties two changes together; 光 and 仅 cut a claim down to one part of it. Both are the written register creeping in, and by HSK 4 roughly half of what you read is written rather than spoken Chinese.

stages.goal: Grant a point without conceding it, and push an example to its limit.
stages.sentence: 尽管连他都不同意，我们还是做了三次。
stages.title: Concession and emphasis
stages.why: 即使…也, 尽管…还是, 不管…都, 连…都, 甚至. Eight patterns that all translate to English 'even', and choosing between them is whether what follows is real, hypothetical, an open case or an extreme. The syllabus spaces them apart on purpose; they are the classic fused memory.

stages.goal: Finish HSK 4: the remaining six hundred words, and the point at which reading stops being decoding.
stages.sentence: 这篇文章我读下去了，没查字典。
stages.title: Finishing HSK 4
stages.why: Mostly vocabulary now. The patterns are in place; what is left is the volume that makes an ordinary newspaper paragraph readable without stopping.

stages.goal: Add, qualify, attribute and doubt — the machinery of saying what you think.
stages.sentence: 在我看来，这个办法不见得可行，不过值得一试。
stages.title: Holding an opinion
stages.why: The densest stretch of grammar in the whole syllabus: 并且, 然而, 不过, 却, 在…看来, 就…而言, 不见得, 可见. Twenty-five points in two hundred and sixty words, because HSK 5 is the level where the language stops reporting facts and starts weighing them.

stages.goal: Say the opposite of what was expected, and draw a conclusion from it.
stages.sentence: 他不但没生气，反而笑了，可见并不在意。
stages.title: Reversal and inference
stages.why: 反而 and 相反 both reverse, 从而 and 总之 both conclude, and 所 turns a verb into the thing it acts on. The written passive 为…所 arrives here too — the first construction that would look wrong spoken aloud.

stages.goal: Suppose the unlikely, and say what would still hold.
stages.sentence: 哪怕只有一个人反对，一旦出问题也是我的责任。
stages.title: Supposing the worst
stages.why: 哪怕, 就算, 一旦, 除非. Four ways to grant a hypothetical, separated by how likely it is and whether the outcome survives it. 一旦 looks forward to a decisive step; 万一 prepares for one nobody wants.

stages.goal: Two hundred and sixty more words. No new patterns — this is the volume that makes a page hold together.
stages.sentence: 这部电影我没看字幕，也跟得上。
stages.title: Reading without stopping
stages.why: An honest stage. The grammar of HSK 5 is behind you and what remains is words, in the order the syllabus reaches them. This is the stretch where a film without subtitles starts to work, and there is no shortcut through it.

stages.goal: Finish HSK 5, and the last two prepositions of reliance: 凭 and 靠.
stages.sentence: 凭这点本事，只能靠自己慢慢来。
stages.title: Finishing HSK 5
stages.why: 凭票入场 and 靠自己 are the same idea in two registers, one on a sign and one in speech. Register is most of what HSK 6 will be about, and this is where noticing it starts.

stages.goal: Twenty-two patterns that belong on a page rather than in a mouth.
stages.sentence: 与其空谈，不如动手；之所以拖延，是因为无人负责。
stages.title: The written register
stages.why: HSK 6 opens with the largest block of grammar since HSK 3, and almost none of it is spoken: 与其…不如, 之所以…是因为, 唯有…才, 岂不, 莫非, 固然, 诚然. The words are not harder; the register is. Say 岂不 out loud in a shop and you have made a joke.

stages.goal: The 免 family, and the purposes it serves.
stages.sentence: 早点说清楚，以免误会；第一次上台，不免紧张。
stages.title: What is avoided, and what cannot be
stages.why: 以便, 以免, 免得, 免不了, 不免, 不禁, 难免. Seven terms sharing two characters between them, meaning by turns 'so that', 'so as not to', 'bound to' and 'could not help'. The syllabus spaces them apart deliberately; met together they collapse into one wrong memory within a week.

stages.goal: Three hundred more words, and the connectives that take an argument one step on.
stages.sentence: 先摸清情况，进而提出办法；等不下去了，索性重做。
stages.title: Going further
stages.why: 进而 and 索性 sit at opposite ends of the same decision: one builds carefully on what came before, the other abandons half-measures. Between them is most of the vocabulary of this stretch.

stages.goal: Say that something is bound to happen, or rather too much, or not necessarily so.
stages.sentence: 这样说未免太重，事情未必如此。
stages.title: Measure and reservation
stages.why: 势必, 未免, 未必, 姑且. Two of them are one character apart and mean opposite things — 未免太严厉 says it went too far, 未必是真的 says it may not be true at all — and they are kept apart in the order for exactly that reason.

stages.goal: Three hundred more words. No new patterns.
stages.sentence: 这一段没有生词了。
stages.title: The long middle
stages.why: The honest part of HSK 6. Two thousand five hundred words is the size of the level and there is no arrangement of them that makes it short. What the ordering can do — and has — is make sure each one leans on characters already held.

stages.goal: The last two frames of formal writing: sweeping in a whole category, and justifying a decision.
stages.sentence: 鉴于时间紧张，凡是未报名的一律不受理。
stages.title: Given, and all of
stages.why: 鉴于 justifies; 凡是 includes without exception. Both are the language of notices, contracts and minutes — the register that HSK 6 exists to make readable.

stages.goal: Three hundred more words, and the end is in sight.
stages.sentence: 坚持到这里的人不多。
stages.title: The last stretch of vocabulary
stages.why: Nothing new to explain. At this point the scheduler is doing most of the work and the only question left is whether you keep turning up.

stages.goal: The end of the official list, and the two literary conditionals that close it.
stages.sentence: 倘若当初没有开始，假如中途放弃，都到不了这里。
stages.title: Finishing HSK 6
stages.why: 倘若 and 假如 are 如果 in a suit, and it is fitting that the last two grammar points on the route are a formal way of saying 'if'. Everything past here is 进阶 — the idiom corpus, the 歇后语, and the sixty thousand dictionary words built from characters you now hold.
